methodology: Local HTTP fixtures, actual installed Google Chrome, clean profiles, unmodified ZIP extractions. Normal native popup blocking and isolated disable-popup-blocking controls. Automatic calls verified without user activation; tab lifecycle, source provenance, observer diagnostics and server receipts measured independently. No Internet-wide success percentage or CPU/RAM benchmark.

provenance.interpretation: These are 54 compatibility and regression assertions in local Chrome fixtures, not a percentage of advertisements or web popups blocked. Four baseline failures change surviving-tab outcomes; six detect incorrect gesture sequence or submitter intent. Both rapid-click tabs remained open in the baseline, so those cases do not demonstrate a second tab being closed.
provenance.automaticControls: All 14 automatic cases asserted navigator.userActivation.isActive=false and hasBeenActive=false before window.open. Separate native-blocker and isolated-lab profiles distinguish Chrome suppression from extension closures.
